consensus.title: Privilege escalation due to truthy authorization check

responses.content:
* [CRITICAL] [AUTH_CRYPTO] Privilege escalation due to truthy authorization check (at `on_login`)
  - Issue: `if user.role == "admin" or "owner":` is parsed as `if (user.role == "admin") or "owner":`. Since the non-empty string `"owner"` is always truthy, every successfully authenticated user—including roles with no administrative privileges—receives `request.session["can_manage"] = True`. Any downstream permission check relying on this session flag will authorize ordinary users to perform management actions.
  - Fix: Compare the role against both allowed values, e.g. `if user.role in ("admin", "owner"):`, and ensure the actual management endpoint also verifies the required authorization rather than trusting this session flag alone.

* [CRITICAL] SECURITY Logic Error in Role Check (at line 16)
  - Issue: The condition `if user.role == "admin" or "owner":` is a classic Python boolean logic bug. The expression evaluates as `(user.role == "admin") or ("owner")`, where the string literal `"owner"` is always truthy. This means ALL users will have `can_manage` set to True, granting administrative privileges to every authenticated user regardless of their actual role.
  - Fix: `if user.role in ("admin", "owner"):`

* [CRITICAL] AUTH_CRYPTO Incorrect role check (on_login function)
  - Issue: The condition `if user.role == "admin" or "owner":` always evaluates to True because the literal string `"owner"` is truthy, granting `request.session["can_manage"] = True` to any user, resulting in unauthorized privilege escalation.
  - Fix: Change to `if user.role == "admin" or user.role == "owner":` or `if user.role in ("admin", "owner"):`.

* [WARNING] [LOGIC] Incorrect condition always evaluates to True (at if user.role == "admin" or "owner":)
  - Issue: The condition `user.role == "admin" or "owner"` is always true because the string "owner" is truthy. This causes `request.session["can_manage"] = True` to execute for every user, regardless of role, leading to unauthorized privilege escalation.
  - Fix: Change the condition to properly check the user's role, e.g., `if user.role in ("admin", "owner"):` or `if user.role == "admin" or user.role == "owner":`.
